name: Trust, legal & compliance
summary: Privacy operations, minors and age rules, AI-in-hiring law, accessibility, the security program, store data-use compliance, the lawyer-review register and a trust centre that shows the user the facts — so a job seeker who hands Kiwiply their whole application history can see exactly who sees it, that nobody applies for them, and that they can take it all and leave in two taps.

epics.name: Legal foundation & lawyer review
epics.goal: Versioned policies with a plain-language changelog, recorded acceptance on every surface, material-change prompts, and one register of every document and question that needs a lawyer (entity: AutomoraLab LLC; PL.1 still open).

epics.name: Privacy operations: data map, export, deletion, retention, subprocessors
epics.goal: A data map that is code, a complete asynchronous export, enumerated erasure with a completeness test, a published retention table, a named subprocessor list with signed DPAs, an AI provider on a no-training tier, and GPC honoured.

epics.name: Minors & age assurance
epics.goal: A neutral 16+ age screen that stores no birth date, under-age handling that works, school/bootcamp org assertions, and high-privacy defaults for 16–17-year-olds.

epics.name: AI-in-hiring law & algorithmic transparency
epics.goal: An AI feature register as code, disclosure and 'why' on every AI output, a sensitive-field firewall that is a test, attestations never ticked, provenance on every output, and the counsel memo on EU AI Act / NYC LL144 / CPPA ADMT.

epics.name: Accessibility program (WCAG 2.2 AA)
epics.goal: One CI gate for every surface, an accessibility contract in @kiwiply/ui, scheduled manual screen-reader audits, an accessible extension drawer, a public statement and an ACR for org procurement.

epics.name: Security program
epics.goal: security.txt and a disclosure policy with safe harbour, HTTP hardening on web/API, supply-chain scanning, a public /security page, an incident and breach-notification runbook, an external pen test, secrets rotation, extension hardening and a SOC 2 readiness path.

epics.name: Store data-use compliance
epics.goal: The extension passes the 2026 Chrome Web Store Limited Use bar: every destination justified by the single purpose, third-party analytics gone, one source of truth for CWS/AMO/Edge with a CI drift check, a public permissions explainer and a per-fill 'what left this page' panel.

epics.name: Trust centre & transparency
epics.goal: A /trust hub rendered from live facts, a privacy nutrition label at signup and in Settings, a personal data-access ledger ('who looked at my data'), a trust-claims register with evidence, and an annual transparency report.

epics.name: Regulatory watch & compliance checks
epics.goal: A quarterly regulatory watch with owners and dates, and a bundle of doc-sync tests in CI so the policy can never promise less than the code does.

ac: docs/design/trust/REGULATORY-WATCH.md: one row per regime (status, our position, next date, owner, last reviewed); reviewed quarterly and at each launch gate; changes become stories in the owning areas
Store policy changes (CWS, AMO, Edge) included
tests: Docs; a CI reminder check fails if 'last reviewed' is older than 120 days
stories.tech: docs/design/trust/REGULATORY-WATCH.md, scripts/check-policies.mjs (shared with T5.8)

stories.title: Compliance doc-sync test bundle in CI (data map, AI register, subprocessors, retention, manifest/permissions, legal content, claims) as one job
stories.story: As a builder I want one CI job named 'compliance' that runs every doc-sync test so that a policy can never promise less than the code does — or more.
stories.genz: The policy is tested like the code.
ac: ci.yml job `compliance` runs DataMapTest, AiFeatureDocSyncTest, SubprocessorCoverageTest, RetentionCatalogueTest, LegalContentSyncTest, ClaimsRegisterTest, check-data-use.mjs, gen-data-map staleness, SecurityTxtTest; required for merge into develop
A short docs/roadmap/COMPLIANCE-CHECKS.md lists what each check guarantees
tests: The job itself; a seeded drift (remove a subprocessor row) fails
stories.tech: .github/workflows/ci.yml, docs/roadmap/COMPLIANCE-CHECKS.md
